name.text: Representation of exponential growth and decay of function

questiontext.text:
Determine whether the function below represents exponential growth, exponential decay, or neither.

  1. \( \displaystyle f(x)={@initial_x@}({@base_x@})^{x}\)

    [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

  2. \( \displaystyle f(t)={@initial_t@}({@base_t@})^{t}\)

    [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

To determine whether the given functions represent exponential growth, exponential decay, or neither, we need to examine the base of the exponential term in each function.

The general form of an exponential function is \( f(x) = a \cdot b^x \), where \(a\) is a constant and \(b\) is the base of the exponent.

  • If \(b > 1\), the function represents exponential growth.
  • If \(0 < b < 1\), the function represents exponential decay.
  • If \(b = 1\) or \(b \leq 0\), it is neither exponential growth nor decay.

Let's analyze each function:

  1. \( \displaystyle f(x)={@initial_x@}({@base_x@})^{x}\)

    In this function, the base \(b = {@base_x@}\)

    {@is_growth@}.

  2. \( \displaystyle f(t)={@initial_t@}({@base_t@})^{t}\)

    In this function, the base \(b = {@base_t@}\).

    {@is_decay@}.
